title: The dairy sector built in the 1990s on imported Holstein cows and imported concentrates is contracting: milk output fell about 16% from its 2021 peak to 2025 and the herd shrinks about 2.5% a year after drought and feed price shocks; the ministry and farmers describe a lasting gap between feed costs and the administered milk price, frozen at 1,340 millimes since late 2022 or early 2023

rootCauses.cause: Early-1990s dairy policy (surtax on imported powder, higher producer price, facilities to import dairy cows, guaranteed concentrate supply mainly by imports) built an intensive Holstein-based herd that depends on purchased feed

The farm-gate milk price is administered by the state and revised by decision, not by cost; it has stayed at 1,340 millimes per litre since November 2022 (ONAGRI) or February 2023 (ministry) while feed costs kept rising
World price surge for feed raw materials and dinar devaluation raised concentrate costs (+35% 2019-2022)
Recurrent droughts and water scarcity cut roughage production and increased dependence on compound feed
The ministry describes a fragmented sector with small herds, which may increase exposure to price and climate shocks (tier C; causal effect not quantified)

sections.heading: Problem
sections.content: Fresh milk production peaked at about 1,462 thousand t in 2021 and fell to 1,230 thousand t in 2025, about 16% lower. Over 2016-2025 the average change was -1.5% a year (SRC-TG-761). The dairy herd was estimated at 360,000 female units in 2024 and has shrunk 2.5% a year since 2015. No livestock census has been run since 2019, so recent herd numbers are estimates (SRC-TG-761). Yield per cow also fell, from about 6,279 kg in 2015 to 5,749 kg in 2024 (SRC-TG-761). Dairy imports grew 21.1% a year in value over 2016-2025, reaching 292.1 million TND in 2025, for a dairy trade deficit of 233.4 million TND (SRC-TG-761). This is the end of a long expansion: production rose from 400 million litres in 1990 to 870 million litres in 2000 under a deliberate policy (SRC-TG-760).

sections.heading: Root causes
sections.content:
**Past decision (legacy).** After a phase of reconstituting milk from imported powder, Tunisia switched in the 1980s-1990s to promoting local milk. From 1983 collection centres received a premium of 20% of the producer price. The take-off of the early 1990s combined several measures: a surtax on imported milk powder, an extended consumer milk subsidy, a higher producer price, facilities to import dairy cows, a "guaranteed regular supply of concentrate feed, mainly through imports", and fodder crop support (SRC-TG-760). The resulting herd is 59% pure-bred Holstein (SRC-TG-761), a breed that depends on concentrates and good forage. Part of the herd growth came from cattle units set up in unsuitable places, such as oases and urban belts, run "landless" with below-standard performance (SRC-TG-760). Production grew from 400 to 730 million litres between 1990 and 1998 (SRC-TG-760). The model was exposed from the start: production fell in the 2001-2002 droughts (SRC-TG-760). Border protection for milk was cut from a nominal rate of 55.8% in 1995 to 3.6% in 2000 (SRC-TG-760). Earlier, the 1989-1995 adjustment programme had already committed to aligning milk prices more closely with world prices and to liberalising milk imports (SRC-TG-921). Price support for milk did not disappear, though. In the late 2000s milk took over half of market price support spending, and milk collection premia were about 40% of input subsidies in 2008-2009 (SRC-TG-710; see FND-TG-921). Milk was a supported product in the 2000s; the current complaint is that the administered price has lagged costs since 2022.

**Administered price against rising costs.** The state sets the minimum farm-gate milk price. It was raised in steps from 736 millimes per litre (January 2015) to 1,340 (SRC-TG-761) and has not moved since late 2022 or early 2023. Over 2019-2022 the sourced numbers do not show a squeeze on their own. The price rose from 945 (October 2019) to 1,340 (November 2022), about +42%, while concentrate prices rose 35% between 2019 and 2022 (SRC-TG-706). The gap shows during 2021-2022, when the price stood at 1,140 (+21% over 2019) as feed costs climbed. It shows again after the freeze, for which no sourced feed cost series was found. The ministry itself describes "a lasting imbalance between production costs and selling prices". It attributes this to the world surge in feed raw material prices and to droughts that cut roughage output and increased dependence on compound feed (SRC-TG-766). UTAP claimed a production cost of 1.85 TND per litre in May 2023 against 1.34 TND paid, a loss of about 500 millimes per litre (SRC-TG-765; tier C, interested party). ITES, discussing the Covid-19 and 2021-2022 input-price shocks and citing an IACE/UTAP 2021 survey, reports some poultry and dairy farmers partly or fully abandoned production (SRC-TG-706).

**Symptom vs cause.** Milk shortages and falling collection are symptoms. The causes are a feed-intensive, import-dependent production model (FND-TG-760), an administered output price that lags input costs, and recurrent drought that removes the cheaper home-grown roughage.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.content:
- Production 2016-2025, read from chart (thousand t): 1408, 1424, 1310, 1352, 1392, 1462, 1330, 1224, 1248, 1230 (SRC-TG-761). The 2025 value and the -1.5% average are confirmed in the table on the same page.
- Herd 360,000 female units in 2024 (211,000 Holstein, 149,000 local and crossbred), -2.5%/yr over 2015-2024. Note: "Le recensement n'a pas été réalisé depuis 2019" (SRC-TG-761).
- A cow with calf cost 7,056 TND in 2024, rising 9.5% a year since 2015 (SRC-TG-761). Rebuilding the herd is therefore expensive.
- Farm-gate milk price path (OEP via ONAGRI), in millimes per litre: 736 (Jan 2015), 766 (Apr 2017), 890 (Jul 2018), 945 (Oct 2019), 1,040 (Jul 2020), 1,140 (Apr 2021), 1,340 (Nov 2022), unchanged in 2024 (SRC-TG-761).
- **Sources disagree on the dates.** ONAGRI gives 1,040 millimes in July 2020 and the last revision in November 2022 (SRC-TG-761). The ministry's answer to parliament, as reported by the press, says the price went from 945 to 1,340 millimes "between August 2020 and February 2023" in three revisions, with the collection premium raised to 115 millimes per litre (SRC-TG-766). Both agree on the current level of 1,340.
- Dairy trade 2025: imports 29.4 thousand t (292.1 million TND) and exports 9.3 thousand t (58.7 million TND). ONAGRI's import penetration is 2.3% of production, but it compares tonnes of dairy products (powder, butter, cheese) with tonnes of fresh milk, not milk equivalent, so it understates dependence. Import value is growing fast (SRC-TG-761).
- In 2022 a fall in barley imports partly caused temporary feed shortages, affecting milk availability and causing light consumer shortages for a few weeks; ITES says intermediary opportunism and some traders’ speculation appear to have worsened the crisis (SRC-TG-706).
- Historical: milk production was 140 million litres in 1970, 400 in 1990 and 870 in 2000 (SRC-TG-760).
- **Herd, yield and production do not reconcile in the ONAGRI fiche.** 360,000 cows at 5,749 kg a year would give about 2.07 million t, against about 1.25 million t produced in 2024 (SRC-TG-761). The female-unit herd probably includes non-lactating animals, or the yield refers to controlled herds only, but the fiche does not say. Herd and yield trends are therefore treated as indicative. A 2026 press report quotes the OEP at about 330,000 female units and UTAP at about 3,580 litres per cow/year; this lends support to the concern that ONAGRI’s 5,749 kg yield is not an all-herd average, but both are tier C and methods differ (SRC-TG-772).

sections.heading: Why confidence is what it is
sections.content:
Medium overall, but split. The contraction of production is solid (high). The herd decline is medium, because there has been no census since 2019 and herd and yield do not reconcile. The size of the price-cost gap after 2022 is low, because it rests on the ministry's description and a UTAP figure. Production, price and trade series come from ONAGRI's official fiche (tier A). Year-by-year chart values are read from labels, but the endpoints match the printed table. Herd figures after 2019 are estimates without a census, which weakens the herd-decline indicator. The cost side is the weak point. The only opened production cost figure is a UTAP statement (tier C), so the size of the price-cost gap is not established by an independent source. The direction of the squeeze is supported by ITES (concentrate +35%, tier B) and by the ministry's own description (tier C press report). The legacy policy account rests on one peer-reviewed synthesis (SRC-TG-760) citing an IAMM evaluation (Bourbouze and Elloumi, 1998) that was not opened.

The brief framed this as a "milk shortage crisis in 2022-2023". The evidence supports a sustained contraction of production and herd, with short shortages in 2022. It does not show a collapse of supply. Fresh milk output in 2025 was about 1.23 million t, about 13% below its 2016 level of 1.41 million t (SRC-TG-761): a decline, not a collapse.

sections.heading: Links to other sectors
sections.content:
- **Water:** the ministry links the crisis to recurrent droughts and water scarcity that cut roughage production (SRC-TG-766). Part of the Holstein herd was installed in oases and peri-urban "landless" units (SRC-TG-760), where forage for cattle competes for scarce irrigation water. The water lane covers oasis aquifers; no source here quantifies water use by dairy forage.
- **Energy:** none found. (Milk cooling and collection use electricity, but no source was found on this as a constraint.)

sections.heading: Leads for phase 2
sections.content:
- Three revisions of the guaranteed minimum milk price (2020-2023) and the collection premium of 115 millimes per litre (SRC-TG-766)
- Feed price caps with the Ministry of Commerce (SRC-TG-766)
- National herd rebuilding programme for milk and red meat (seen in press headlines, not opened; https://businessnews.com.tn/2026/09/24/lait-et-viandes-rouges-93-millions-de-dinars-pour-reconstruire-le-cheptel/1419964/) and the national fodder production plan (SRC-TG-766)
- Six ministerial councils on the dairy sector, 2020-2024 (SRC-TG-766)
- Dual-purpose strains and local breeds as an alternative to Holstein imports (raised in SRC-TG-760)
- GIVLAIT, the interprofessional group for red meat and milk (www.givlait.com.tn), seen on the ONAGRI site

resolvedSources.title: La sécurité alimentaire de la Tunisie à l'horizon 2035
resolvedSources.publisher: Institut Tunisien des Études Stratégiques (ITES), hosted by ONAGRI
resolvedSources.extracts:
Page numbers are PDF page numbers (printed numbers differ). Study dated December 2023, addressed to the President of the Republic.

PDF p. 27 (policy review 1960-1970):

> Pour le développement de la production de céréales, un Office des Céréales (OC) a été créé en 1962

English gloss: to develop cereal production, an Office des Céréales was created in 1962.

PDF p. 32 (price policy periods, after Khaldi and Naili 1995):

> Le blocage des prix et des salaires (1960-1970) : au cours de cette période, la politique de l'Etat en matière de prix à la production consistait en la fixation et le maintien des prix des produits agricoles à un niveau bas.

> La mise en place des subventions (1970-1984) : en 1971, la Caisse Générale de Compensation (CGC) est créée pour gérer un système de

English gloss: 1960-1970, the state fixed producer prices of agricultural products at a low level; 1970-1984, subsidies set up — in 1971 the CGC was created to manage a subsidy system.

PDF p. 33:

> Les seuls produits qui continuent après à être subventionnés sont les céréales d'alimentation humaine, l'huile

English gloss: after structural adjustment, the only products still subsidised are cereals for human consumption, (vegetable) oil [and others].

PDF p. 33 (citing INS 2013, analysis of the impact of food subsidies on poverty):

> qu'en 2010, seules 9,2 % des subventions sont orientées aux ménages les plus démunis, 60,5 % aux ménages de la classe moyenne, 7,5 % à la population aisée, alors que 22,8 % sont transférés hors ménages, notamment vers les entreprises de restauration hors foyer.

English gloss: in 2010 only 9.2% of subsidies went to the poorest households, 60.5% to middle-class households, 7.5% to the well-off, and 22.8% outside households, notably to out-of-home catering businesses.

PDF p. 52 (stability of access):

> Selon l'INC, le gaspillage du pain par les ménages a atteint les 900.000 pains/j, ce qui correspond à une valeur moyenne de l'ordre de 100 millions DT/an.

English gloss: according to the INC, household bread waste reached 900,000 loaves a day, worth about 100 million TND a year (no year given).

PDF p. 53:

> Le taux de dépendance vis-à-vis des céréales importées reste en moyenne de l'ordre de 60%, soit : • 40% pour le blé dur ; • 80% pour le blé tendre ; • 50% pour l'orge

English gloss: dependence on imported cereals averages about 60%: 40% durum wheat, 80% soft wheat, 50% barley.

PDF p. 54:

> La production céréalière connait une légère tendance à la baisse, malgré les investissements et les soutiens de l'Etat. [...] Elle est en grande partie issue des cultures pluviales (seulement 10% en irrigué) et reste soumise aux aléas climatiques.

> La moyenne se situe autour de 17 millions de Tonnes durant la période 2010-2018. Les rendements n'excèdent pas les 25 q/ha pour le blé dur, 21 q/ha pour le blé tendre et 16 q/ha pour l'orge avec une moyenne de 18q/ha pour la même période.

> La production de blé dur prédomine et progresse vu son adaptation aux conditions locales (+27% entre 2010-2018), contre un recul du blé tendre (-25%).

English gloss: cereal production shows a slight downward trend despite state investment and support; it is mostly rainfed (only 10% irrigated) and exposed to climate hazards. Average around "17 million tonnes" (sic) over 2010-2018. Yields do not exceed 25 q/ha durum, 21 q/ha soft wheat, 16 q/ha barley, average 18 q/ha. Durum production up 27% over 2010-2018, soft wheat down 25%.

PDF p. 55:

> La part de l'office des céréales dans la collecte physique a fortement diminué passant de 32% en 2005 à 2% en 2012, au profit d'opérateurs privés désormais majoritaires (58%) et des sociétés mutuelles de service agricoles (SMSA) (40%).

English gloss: OC's share of physical collection fell from 32% in 2005 to 2% in 2012, in favour of private operators (58%) and agricultural service cooperatives (40%).

PDF p. 116 (printed p. 114; page corrected by source-verifier, previously given as p. 121), trend micro-scenario (H1, "au fil de l'eau"), horizon 2035, V12-H1:

> La dépendance au marché international se poursuit pour les produits de base et les intrants (Taux de dépendance moyen des céréales 57% dont le Blé tendre avec 84%, le blé dur 41% et l'orge 51%)

PDF p. 108, footnote 94 to the same figures: (footnote text not found again by text search on re-check; page unconfirmed)

> Maintien de la moyenne des dix dernières années. Source : Observatoire Tunisien de l'Economie, 2023. Dépendance aux importations de blé.

English gloss: in the trend scenario to 2035, average cereal dependence stays at 57% (soft wheat 84%, durum 41%, barley 51%); the footnote says this is the ten-year average held constant (source Observatoire Tunisien de l'Economie, 2023).

### Livestock feed extracts (added for FND-TG-760/761)

PDF p. 55:

> sachant que la demande augmentera de 50% pour les céréales et doublera pour les aliments de bétail (SOLIDAR et PAM, 2020)

English gloss: by 2035 demand will rise 50% for cereals and double for livestock feed (citing SOLIDAR and WFP, 2020).

PDF p. 66 (section II.2.1.1 Disponibilité, Covid-19 and 2021-2022 shocks):

> les aliments de bétail, qui sont en grande partie importés (30% des besoins en graines de maïs, de blé fourrager, de tourteau de Soja et d'orge). La valeur des importations en 2021 a enregistré un accroissement significatif par rapport à 2019 (Fig. 1), soit 75% contre 26%. Ceci résulte essentiellement de l'accroissement des quantités importées, (surtout du tourteau de soja de 85% et de l'orge de 64%), mais aussi de la volatilité de leur prix sur le marché mondial (Fig. 2) et de la dévaluation du dinar tunisien. Les augmentations des prix ont atteint en 2021 un accroissement de 48% pour le maïs, 30% pour l'orge et 18% pour le soja.

English gloss: livestock feed is largely imported ("30% of needs" for maize, feed wheat, soybean meal and barley, as printed). The value of feed imports in 2021 rose 75% over 2019, mainly because of higher import volumes (soybean meal +85%, barley +64%), but also world price volatility and the devaluation of the Tunisian dinar. Prices rose in 2021 by 48% for maize, 30% for barley and 18% for soya.

> Vu l'augmentation drastique du cours de la matière première, les prix du concentré ont enregistré une hausse de 35% en 2022 par rapport à 2019. Il est prévu que la tendance haussière des prix du concentré va se poursuivre à un rythme plus rapide, ce qui constituera une menace sérieuse pour le secteur de l'élevage.

English gloss: concentrate feed prices rose 35% in 2022 compared with 2019; the upward trend is expected to continue faster, a serious threat to livestock farming.

> D'autres ont abandonné partiellement ou totalement leurs activités (tel le cas pour l'élevage avicole et laitier).

English gloss: some farmers partly or fully abandoned their activity (as in poultry and dairy farming).

PDF p. 66, Covid-19 and 2021-2022 shocks (continuation):

> D'autres ont abandonné partiellement ou totalement leurs activités (tel le cas pour l'élevage avicole et laitier).

English gloss: some poultry and dairy farmers partly or fully abandoned their activity in the context of the Covid-19 and input-price shocks; the study cites the IACE/UTAP 2021 survey.

PDF pp. 69-70 (2022 supply disruption):

> Concrètement, les chiffres montrent que c'est surtout l'orge qui a subi de fortes baisses à l'importation d'où l'explication, en partie, de l'indisponibilité temporaire de quantités suffisantes d'aliments de bétail qui a agi sur la disponibilité du lait et autres sources alimentaires de protéines animales.

> Au niveau du citoyen, ceci s'est ressenti sous forme de légères pénuries durant quelques semaines.

> L'opportunisme des intermédiaires et la spéculation de certains commerçants semblent avoir accentué cette crise temporaire.

English gloss: barley imports fell sharply (2022), partly explaining a temporary feed shortage affecting milk and other animal protein availability; consumers felt light shortages for a few weeks. Intermediary opportunism and some traders’ speculation appear to have worsened the crisis.
resolvedSources.notes: ITES is a state think tank attached to the Presidency; tier B. The 2010-2018 production sentence mixes units ("17 millions de Tonnes" is almost certainly quintals, i.e. about 1.7 Mt; elsewhere "26 MT" for 2009); it is quoted but not used as an indicator. The 2035 "projection" is a scenario assumption (ten-year average held constant), not a model. The CGC creation year here (1971) differs from the World Bank (1970, SRC-TG-705).

resolvedSources.extracts:
Chapter subtitle, p. 259 (printed):

> Tunisia does not have an agricultural policy; rather it has a food security policy, which goes against the potential of its agricultural sector

Box 9.1 discussion, pp. 261-262:

> not have a strong comparative advantage in cereals, which are intensive in land and are socially less profitable than arboriculture, fruits, and vegetables (box 9.1).

> Tunisia is also competitive in durum wheat (rain-fed and irrigated) and was also competitive in irrigated soft wheat when the international prices spiked in 2008, such that temporarily it became profitable to produce soft wheat in Tunisia. The competitiveness in soft wheat is limited to the irrigated areas and areas in the north and northwest regions where the rainfall is more favorable (not shown).

Section 9.2, p. 263:

> Market price support is carried out mostly through the implementation of a guaranteed minimum price for producers of cereals and intervention purchases carried out by the state marketing boards for milk, sugar beet, and tobacco.

> Cereals (soft wheat, durum wheat, and barley) account for a further third of the expenditure on market price support.

p. 265:

> pays inadequate quality bonuses for cereals, and caps the prices of processed foods.

p. 266:

> In 2009 the budgetary cost of food subsidies was approximately 1.5 percent of GDP, and this amount increased to over three percent of GDP in 2012 (table 9.3).

> Using a linear programming model [...] the World Bank estimates that nearly 70 percent of farms would gain from the removal of price distortions in the agricultural sector (table 9.5). resolvedSources.title: Analyse comparée de la dynamique de la production laitière dans les pays du Maghreb
resolvedSources.publisher: Cahiers Agricultures, vol. 16, n° 4 (Sraïri, Ben Salem, Bourbouze, Elloumi, Faye, Madani, Yakhlef), doi 10.1684/agr.2007.0118
resolvedSources.extracts:
p. 254 (Tunisia section; the authors cite Bourbouze and Elloumi, 1998):

> En Tunisie, les deux approches ont été expérimentées. Après une période durant laquelle la politique a favorisé la reconstitution du lait à partir de poudre importée, une politique d'encouragement de la production et de la collecte locales a été adoptée. Elle est intervenue après l'aggravation du déficit en lait et la hausse de sa facture d'importation (tableau 6). À partir de 1983, une prime correspondant à 20 % du prix payé aux producteurs a été attribuée aux centres de collecte. Mais le décollage effectif ne va avoir lieu qu'à partir du début des années 1990, avec des mesures plus concrètes comprenant les volets suivants (Bourbouze et Elloumi, 1998) : instauration d'une surtaxe sur la poudre de lait importée ; extension de la subvention à la consommation du lait ; augmentation du prix du lait à la production ; facilités pour l'importation de vaches de races laitières ; garantie d'un approvisionnement régulier en aliments concentrés surtout par importations ; encouragement des cultures fourragères en sec et en irrigué. L'ensemble de ces mesures s'est traduit par une augmentation notable de la production de lait frais. Par ailleurs, à la fin des années 1990, une diminution progressive de la protection de la production locale est intervenue (tableau 7)

English gloss: Tunisia first reconstituted milk from imported powder, then switched to promoting local production and collection after the milk deficit and import bill worsened. From 1983 collection centres received a premium of 20% of the producer price. Real take-off came in the early 1990s with: a surtax on imported milk powder; extended consumer milk subsidy; higher producer milk price; facilities to import dairy-breed cows; a guaranteed regular supply of concentrate feed, mainly through imports; and support for rainfed and irrigated fodder crops. Production rose markedly. From the late 1990s protection of local production was progressively reduced.

p. 254, Tableau 6 "Environnement humain et performances laitières en Tunisie de 1970 à 2000" (columns 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000; rows re-aligned, see Notes):

> Population bovine totale (en millions) 0,70 0,60 0,62 0,78
> Production laitière (en millions de litres) 140 212 400 870

English gloss: total cattle 0.70 / 0.60 / 0.62 / 0.78 million; milk production 140 / 212 / 400 / 870 million litres in 1970 / 1980 / 1990 / 2000.

p. 254, Tableau 7 (milk protection rates in Tunisia, after CIHEAM and IRESA 2002), years 1995 to 2000:

> TPN* 55,8 62,2 21,4 19,8 15,3 3,6
> TPE** 128,7 146,8 40,7 38,2 28,9 8,3

English gloss: nominal protection rate of milk fell from 55.8% (1995) to 3.6% (2000); effective protection from 128.7% to 8.3%.

p. 256 (Tunisia section, continued; first sentence follows "Les mesures adoptées à la fin des années 1980 ont abouti à l'instauration d'une" at the foot of p. 255):

> filière plus organisée et à la modification de la structure génétique du cheptel. Par conséquent, une croissance importante et soutenue de la production a été enregistrée (de 400 à 730 millions de litres entre 1990 et 1998) (Lahmar et al., 2005), conjuguée à une extension du réseau de collecte, une augmentation de la capacité de transformation et une diversification de la gamme des produits transformés.

English gloss: the measures of the late 1980s produced a better organised sector and changed the genetic structure of the herd; production grew strongly, from 400 to 730 million litres between 1990 and 1998, with a wider collection network and more processing capacity.

> Toutefois, à partir de 2001-2002, la production a décru, en raison de la succession d'épisodes de sécheresse, mettant en relief la forte dépendance vis-à-vis des aléas climatiques. L'augmentation des effectifs de vaches laitières spécialisées est due en grande partie à l'implantation d'élevages bovins dans des régions qui ne s'y prêtent pas vraiment (oasis et ceintures urbaines). Dans ces situations en « hors-sol », les performances de productivité des vaches et la qualité du lait sont en deçà des standards (Lahmar et al., 2003).

English gloss: from 2001-2002 production fell because of successive droughts, showing strong dependence on climate. Much of the increase in specialised dairy cows came from cattle units set up in regions not suited to them (oases, urban belts); in these "landless" units cow productivity and milk quality are below standard.

p. 253 (heifer imports; this passage belongs to the MOROCCO section, it follows Moroccan heifer-import studies and precedes "l'expérience marocaine"; not used for Tunisia):

> L'interdiction de ces importations à la suite de la crise de l'encéphalopathie spongiforme bovine (ESB), entre 2000 et 2004, a mis en relief leur importance, les éleveurs ne maîtrisant pas la préparation du renouvellement

English gloss: the ban on these (heifer) imports after the BSE crisis, 2000-2004, showed how much the herd depended on them, since farmers did not master raising their own replacements.

p. 256 (Conclusion, Maghreb-wide):

> Par ailleurs, les achats de concentrés et l'irrigation, peinent à contrecarrer les effets des aléas climatiques et du manque de fourrages, ce qui plombe les marges des éleveurs. De même, la réflexion sur les politiques d'amélioration génétique, basées jusqu'ici sur les importations de vaches Holstein, n'a pas encore intégré ni les possibilités d'acclimatation d'autres souches à double finalité ni le poids des races locales.

English gloss: concentrate purchases and irrigation struggle to offset climate shocks and the lack of fodder, squeezing farm margins. Breeding policy, based so far on importing Holstein cows, has not considered dual-purpose strains or local breeds.
resolvedSources.notes: Peer-reviewed synthesis. In the `-layout` text extraction of Tableau 6 the row labels are shifted by one line: the values 0,70/0,60/0,62/0,78 sit beside the label "Production laitière" but are cattle numbers in millions, and 140/212/400/870 are milk production in million litres (consistent with the Tunisia text on p. 256, which gives 400 to 730 million litres for 1990-1998 and with the scale of Figure 1). The price rows of Tableau 6 were not used because their alignment could not be confirmed. Tableau 1 (1999 herd structure) was not used for Tunisia: its columns could not be matched reliably. The conclusion is Maghreb-wide, not Tunisia-specific.

resolvedSources.title: Crise du lait en Tunisie : sécheresse, hausse des coûts et fragilités structurelles pointées du doigt
resolvedSources.extracts:
Article of 3 August 2026 reporting the Ministry of Agriculture's written answer to a question from members of the Assemblée des représentants du peuple (body text):

> Dans une réponse à une question écrite adressée par des députés à l'Assemblée des représentants du peuple (ARP), le département a pointé les répercussions des changements climatiques, notamment les sécheresses récurrentes et la rareté de l'eau, qui ont réduit la production de fourrages grossiers et accentué la dépendance des éleveurs aux aliments composés. À cela s'ajoute la flambée sans précédent des prix des matières premières fourragères sur les marchés mondiaux, créant un déséquilibre durable entre les coûts de production et les prix de vente. Le ministère a également relevé des fragilités structurelles, dont l'éparpillement du secteur et la petite taille des troupeaux, qui exposent davantage les petits éleveurs aux chocs économiques et climatiques.

English gloss: the ministry cited recurrent droughts and water scarcity, which cut roughage (forage) production and increased farmers' dependence on compound feed; an unprecedented surge in world prices of feed raw materials, creating a lasting imbalance between production costs and selling prices; and structural weaknesses (fragmented sector, small herds).

> Ces réunions ont abouti à plusieurs décisions, notamment la révision à trois reprises du prix minimum garanti du lait à la production, passé de 945 millimes à 1.340 millimes le litre entre août 2020 et février 2023, ainsi que l'augmentation de la prime de collecte à 115 millimes le litre au profit des collecteurs, des centres de refroidissement et des industriels.

English gloss: six ministerial councils (2020-2024) revised the guaranteed minimum farm-gate milk price three times, from 945 to 1,340 millimes per litre between August 2020 and February 2023, and raised the collection premium to 115 millimes per litre.

> Par ailleurs, en coordination avec le ministère du Commerce, les prix des aliments pour bétail ont été plafonnés pour limiter l'impact de la hausse des coûts sur les éleveurs et préserver le cheptel. Le ministère a aussi mentionné l'élaboration d'un plan national de promotion de la production fourragère

English gloss: feed prices were capped together with the Ministry of Commerce; a national plan to promote fodder production is being prepared.
resolvedSources.notes: Tier C (press, wire copy from TAP), but it reports an official ministry answer to parliament; the original answer was not found online. The same text was carried by La Presse via AllAfrica (https://fr.allafrica.com/stories/202608030516.html). Dates conflict with ONAGRI (SRC-TG-761), which gives 1,040 millimes in July 2020 and the last revision in November 2022. Extracts checked against the raw HTML.

resolvedSources.title: Lait et viandes rouges : 93 millions de dinars pour reconstruire le cheptel
resolvedSources.extracts:
Article of 24 September 2026, reporting an interview on Mosaïque FM with Sana Zitouni, ingénieure générale and sous-directrice at the Office de l'élevage et des pâturages (OEP), and earlier statements by UTAP (body text):

> Selon les données du ministère de l'Agriculture citées par Sana Zitouni, le cheptel bovin national a reculé d'environ 20%. Elle a toutefois insisté sur la méthode utilisée pour mesurer cette évolution, alors que d'autres statistiques disponibles font apparaître des baisses différentes.

> Pour le lait, l'État vise une hausse de 11% de la production nationale afin d'atteindre environ 1,4 million de tonnes à l'horizon 2030.

> Le cheptel bovin devrait, lui, passer d'environ 330.000 à 363.000 unités femelles.

> La contribution directe de l'État au programme est évaluée à environ 93 millions de dinars, selon Sana Zitouni.

> Il avançait alors une baisse de 30% du cheptel, contre les 20% retenus par le ministère selon la méthode de comptabilisation exposée jeudi par Sana Zitouni.

> Il estimait le coût de production d'un litre de lait à environ 1,7 dinar, soit davantage que le prix payé au producteur.

> Il pointait également la faiblesse de la productivité, estimant le rendement moyen à environ 3.580 litres de lait par vache et par an

English gloss:
- According to ministry data cited by the OEP, the national cattle herd has fallen by about 20%. Other statistics show different declines, depending on the method used.
- The national herd rebuilding programme, part of the 2026-2030 plan, aims to raise milk output by 11% to about 1.4 million t by 2030. It aims to take the cattle herd from about 330,000 to 363,000 female units, with a direct state contribution of about 93 million TND.
- UTAP's economic adviser (Fathi Ben Khelifa, early August 2026) put the herd decline at 30%, the production cost at about 1.7 TND per litre (above the producer price) and the average yield at about 3,580 litres per cow per year.
resolvedSources.notes: Tier C: press. It reports an OEP official, who is closer to official data, and the farmers' union, an interested party. The base year of the 20% and 30% declines is not given. The herd figure of about 330,000 female units differs from ONAGRI's 360,000 for 2024 (SRC-TG-761). The UTAP yield of about 3,580 l per cow differs from ONAGRI's 5,749 kg. Extracts checked against the raw HTML.

resolvedSources.title: Republic of Tunisia - Agriculture Sector Adjustment Loan II (Loan 3078-TUN), Implementation Completion Report (Report No. 15355)
resolvedSources.publisher: World Bank, Natural Resources and Environment Division, Maghreb and Iran Department, MENA Region
resolvedSources.extracts:
Executive summary, para. iii (reform areas of the Medium-Term Agricultural Sector Adjustment Programme, MTASAP):

> parastatal reforms: divestiture to the private sector of numerous activities of the Cereals Marketing Board (OC), the National Edible Oil Board (ONH) and the Livestock and Pastures Board (OEP) [...] pricing and marketing: adjustment of prices for cereals and milk to keep them more closely aligned with world prices, the introduction of more market driven prices for beef, the reduction of input subsidies, and the liberalization of meat and milk imports

Para. v:

> an analysis prepared by the Bank before appraisal [...] made it clear that the fiscal balance and sector efficiency measures sought under the ASAL II would result in marginally negative sector growth and incomes for farmers. The President's Report did not present these results because of concern that doing so would weaken the support of the key constituency for the Loan, the Ministry of Agriculture (MOA)

Para. vi:

> The Loan achieved its fiscal objectives since budget costs of subsidies for inputs and credit were substantially reduced -- from 73 to 15 million DT for inputs financed through the General Compensation Fund, through a 40 percent real increase in irrigation tariffs, and a reduction by two-thirds of budget allocations to finance rural credit subsidies [...] Parastatal reform was generally successful in disengaging the organizations from non-core activities, but much less so in achieving greater efficiency through increasing competition from the private sector on a more level playing field, particularly for domestic cereals collection and beef imports [...] wheats continue to be overprotected by restrictive import policy.

Para. 13 (cereals collection):

> in practice very little progress is evident in transferring cereals collection to the private sector. Only three new private participants in cereals collection have emerged, and their activities have remained limited. Risks remain large as long as the OC retains both its role a direct competitor in grain collection and also regulator of the effort to promote private collection.

Para. 15:

> Administered producer prices for soft and hard wheat remained high compared with the agreed formula, while barley producer prices have tracked the formula more closely.

Para. 26:

> The inputs involved were fertilizers, animal feeds, improved cereals seeds, seed potatoes and the herbicide 2-4-D. This objective was fully met, with subsidies either substantially reduced or eliminated. The CGC is the financing mechanism for these subsidies, which peaked at DT 73 million in the drought of 1989 but fell below DT 15 million by 1993.

Para. 27:

> Subsidies for three of the four principal types of fertilizer used in Tunisia have been eliminated. Subsidy reduction began with freeing distribution margins with the 1987/88 campaign, and since 1991 by removal of remaining product subsidies (1991 for Super 16, 1992 for Ammonitre 33, and 1993 for DAP). Only Super 45, which accounts for roughly one-quarter of the total quantities of fertilizer applied, still benefits from a (declining) subsidy. [...] For the 1986-92 period, the increase in real prices of fertilizers averaged 6% annually.

Para. 28:

> Overall subsidies for animal feed peaked in the drought of 1989 at 49 million dinar (current prices) before falling to 4 million dinars in 1992-93.

Para. 13 (continued):

> Transfer of OC facilities to the private sector has proved to be unsuccessful because of the lack of interest linked to a condition in the cahier de charges requiring that all existing personnel be maintained by new management.

Para. 16:

> It eliminated the subsidy for transport cost equalization for cereals, and regarding storage, the Government tested, then implemented an approach for private storage, with the introduction of monthly payments for private storage intended to simulate average seasonal price movements. In conjunction with investment incentives, the promotion of private storage of cereals has proven successful

Para. 18 (olive oil):

> new legislation was passed in 1994 that brought much more extensive liberalization to olive oil exports. [...] Nevertheless, the exporters remain concerned about the ambiguous position of the ONH's which mixes elements of partnership, through provision of services and private sector support, and competition, largely through the ONH's own exports to the European market

Paras. 19-20 (milk):

> a condition of effectiveness was elimination of quantitative restrictions on imports of powdered milk and imposition of a variable levy necessary to provide 15% nominal protection according to an agreed moving average formula. [...] The variable levy was implemented in 1990, and subsequently revised in 1991 and 1993. No adjustments have occurred in the variable levy, or in producer support prices, since 1993.

Para. 23 (beef):

> El Louhoum still accounts for about half of beef imports. [...] In 1994 it was obliged to purchase all live cattle presented to it at a fixed price. El Louhoum continues to benefit from subsidies, does not pay the variable levy on meat imports that the private sector is obliged to pay, and sells its products into its own retail structure with prices that are administratively fixed.

Para. 28 (continued):

> This consisted almost entirely of subsidies on barley, as subsidies on corn were eliminated in 1992 and those on soybean meal in 1993.

Para. 28 (drought feed policy):

> Barley is used to compensate pastoralists for grazing land that is taken out of use during rehabilitation programs, and also small livestock farmers during drought years with the intention of maintaining herd sizes and stabilizing incomes. Corn and soybean meal benefit poultry raisers and also dairy operations, mostly on larger scale farms.

English gloss: the report describes subsidised barley as drought support intended to maintain smallholder herds and compensate pastoralists; corn and soybean meal are used by poultry and dairy, especially larger farms.

Para. 31 (irrigation tariffs):

> The tariffs vary by Region, but averaged 41 millimes /m3 in 1993. This is about 75 percent of the costs of operations and maintenance in the old MOA definition, which does not yet include amortisation and provisioning for repair of civil works and equipment within the perimeter, and about 63 percent of operations and maintenance costs which include these latter components.

Para. 59:

> The sustainability of these subsidy reductions does not seem in doubt: there was no backtracking on the reductions during the subsequent droughts in 1994 and 1995.

Para. 62 (updated multi-market model):

> the realized price policy changes alone would have decreased value added by 1.3 percent [...] there was a small decline, under 1 percent per annum, in real incomes, with the exception of the low income group in the north and center of the country, for whom incomes increased.

Para. 63:

> The DGPDIA has analyzed income trends for four typical farm types ranging from 5 to 80 hectares during the adjustment period. [...] Net incomes derived from the models are stagnant at best for the smaller farm types, and decline for the largest representative farm from 1989 levels.
resolvedSources.notes: Bank self-evaluation, covering 1989-1995. Para. 60 admits monitoring data were largely not collected, so income effects rest on a model and on four representative farm budgets, not on observed household incomes. OCR from scanned original; spelling errors corrected in extracts.

relatedItems.title: Tunisian livestock runs on imported feed: all maize and soybeans and, in drought years, most barley come from abroad, so world prices, the dinar and import disruptions pass straight into farm costs

The state cereal system (Office des Céréales monopoly, decreed prices, CGC subsidies) built in 1962-1971 now strains public finances and blunts market signals
